text: David left there and escaped to the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and his father's whole household heard of it, they went down to him there.
Everyone in distress, everyone in debt, everyone bitter in spirit gathered to him, and he became their commander. About four hundred men were with him.
From there David went to Mizpeh in Moab and said to the king of Moab, "Please let my father and mother come and stay with you until I know what God will do for me."
So he left them with the king of Moab, and they stayed with him the whole time David was in the stronghold.
But the prophet Gad said to David, "Do not stay in the stronghold. Go to the land of Judah." So David left and went to the forest of Hereth.
Saul heard that David and the men with him had been discovered. Saul was sitting at Gibeah under the tamarisk tree on the height, spear in hand, with all his servants standing around him.

versions.text: Saul heard that David and the men with him had been located. Saul was sitting at Gibeah under the tamarisk tree on the height, spear in hand, with all his servants standing around him.
versions.explanation: "Had been located" sounds clinical and modern; "had been discovered" better matches נוֹדַע (was made known) and reads more naturally aloud.

text: Saul said to the servants standing around him, "Listen now, men of Benjamin! Will the son of Jesse give all of you fields and vineyards? Will he make all of you commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds?

Yet all of you have conspired against me, and no one told me when my own son made a covenant with the son of Jesse. Not one of you is concerned for me or tells me that my son has stirred up my servant against me, to lie in wait, as he does today."
Then Doeg the Edomite, who was standing with Saul's servants, answered, "I saw the son of Jesse come to Nob, to Ahimelech son of Ahitub.
Ahimelech inquired of the LORD for him, gave him provisions, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine."
The king sent for Ahimelech the priest, son of Ahitub, and for his father's whole household, the priests at Nob, and they all came to the king.
Saul said, "Listen now, son of Ahitub." He answered, "Here I am, my lord."

Saul said to him, "Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse—giving him bread and a sword and inquiring of God for him, so that he could rise against me and lie in wait, as he does today?"
Ahimelech answered the king, "Who among all your servants is as trustworthy as David? He is the king's son-in-law, he obeys your every command, and he is honored in your house.

versions.text: Ahimelech answered the king, "Who among all your servants is as trustworthy as David? He is the king's son-in-law, captain of your bodyguard, and honored in your house.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads וְסָר אֶל־מִשְׁמַעְתֶּךָ, "and turns aside to (i.e., heeds) your obedience/command." "Captain of your bodyguard" rests on an emendation (שַׂר for סָר) and imports an office not in the received text; rendering it as obedience to the king's orders follows the Hebrew.

text: Is today the first time I have inquired of God for him? Far be it from me! Let the king not charge his servant or anyone in my father's household with anything, for your servant knew nothing at all about this whole matter, great or small.

versions.text: Was that day the first time I inquired of God for him? Far be it from me! Let the king not charge his servant or anyone in my father's household with anything, for your servant knew nothing at all about this whole matter, great or small."
versions.explanation: הַיּוֹם means "today"; Ahimelech is arguing that inquiring for David was his ongoing, customary practice, not a one-time act on some past day. The present-tense rendering preserves his defense.

text: But the king said, "You shall surely die, Ahimelech—you and your father's whole household."

And the king ordered the guards standing beside him, "Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because they too have sided with David. They knew he was fleeing and did not tell me." But the king's servants would not raise a hand to strike down the priests of the LORD.
Then the king said to Doeg, "You turn and strike down the priests." So Doeg the Edomite turned and struck them down. That day he killed eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod.
He also put Nob, the town of the priests, to the sword—men and women, children and infants, oxen, donkeys, and sheep.
But one son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped and fled to David.
Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.
Then David said to Abiathar, "That day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, I knew he would be sure to tell Saul. I am responsible for every life in your father's household.
Stay with me; do not be afraid. The one who seeks my life seeks yours as well. With me you will be safe."
